title: Bitcoin and Ether edge higher as bank rules change and portfolio reaches $72,400
paragraphs: Bitcoin rose about 0.8% to $77,820, while Ether gained 1.1% to roughly $2,268. The broader market was mixed: XRP and BNB edged higher, while Solana slipped 0.4%. That modest rebound follows a difficult October, when Bitcoin lost about 7.3%. The latest completed US spot Bitcoin ETF session recorded $643 million in net withdrawals. Those redemptions and the Binance security crisis remain significant background pressures, even as the largest coins recover some ground.

The FBI attributed the theft of more than $6 billion from Binance to North Korea's TraderTraitor actors. Its new advisory says investigators observed stolen assets being converted primarily into Ether and asked exchanges, DeFi services and infrastructure operators to block transactions linked to listed addresses. This extends the response beyond the exchange itself. Attempts to move the proceeds through swaps and other services could expose additional platforms to compliance and operational disruption.

Canada's revised bank crypto framework is now taking effect for institutions whose fiscal year ends in October. OSFI will recognize eligible hedges across regulated exchanges when calculating capital requirements and exclude qualifying client-clearing derivative exposures from the Group 2 exposure limit. These are targeted changes to the cost and capacity of serving crypto clients. They could make matched trading and clearing more practical for banks, while capital requirements and prudential safeguards remain in place.

Gulf diplomacy also remains relevant to crypto's macro backdrop. Reuters reported that Iranian negotiators met Qatari mediators in Doha, with contacts coordinated with Washington, as officials sought to prevent renewed fighting. Iran's proposals still tie reopening the Strait of Hormuz to conditions including relief from the blockade and access to frozen assets. For markets, the risk is that continued disruption sustains energy costs and inflation pressure. The talks provide no basis yet to assume that shipping conditions or interest-rate expectations will normalize.

Our on-chain portfolio is about $72,384: $11,982 in the active treasury and $60,402 in the cold-storage Safe. The combined marked value increased about $725, or 1.0%, from the previous update. The Safe's 26.74 million liquid ARC tokens are worth roughly $47,581, about 66% of the total, before counting ARC inside liquidity pools. Its largest pool holds WETH and ARC and is worth about $9,892. ARC concentration remains the main portfolio risk.

In the active treasury, Beefy increased from about $1,751 to $2,346, while liquid wallet assets fell from $6,125 to $5,605. Beefy now displays a USDC/cbHYPE position worth about $563 alongside its other pools. Across both wallets, Aave borrowing totals about $3,141 against $7,753 of supplied WETH, with health factors of 2.36 and 1.89. The much smaller Fluid position has about $153 of net value and $1,062 of debt; its 1.03 health factor leaves little liquidation headroom.
